clue.text: Dubious sort with alcoholic drink on platform

indicators.note: something dubious is not straight or reliable, so the word beside it is not to be trusted in its given order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
rum is a spirit distilled from sugar cane

explanation.surface: A shady character stands on a stage holding a glass of something strong.
explanation.definitionFit: A rostrum is a raised stand from which a speaker addresses an audience.

clue.text: Newspaper left on top of an overcoat

blocks.note: a rag is a disparaging word for a newspaper
L is the abbreviation for left
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone has left a newspaper lying on their coat.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, 'on top of' simply puts the first pieces above the last.
explanation.definitionFit: A raglan is a loose overcoat whose sleeves run up to the collar, named after Lord Raglan.

clue.text: Holiday-maker holding up small scuttle

blocks.note: S is the abbreviation for small
a camper is someone holidaying in a tent or caravan

explanation.surface: A tourist props up a little coal scuttle.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue, the holiday-maker holding up the small one sits beneath it. 'Scuttle' looks like a coal bucket but is the verb meaning hurry.
explanation.definitionFit: To scamper and to scuttle both mean to run with quick, short steps.

clue.text: Dickens character, impolite penning note

indicators.note: penning means shutting in, as animals in a pen, so one piece is enclosed by the other

blocks.note: rude means impolite
G is a musical note

explanation.surface: A Dickens figure writes something rude.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penning' fits a novelist writing, but it means enclosing. Barnaby Rudge is the title character of a Dickens novel.
explanation.definitionFit: Barnaby Rudge is the hero of Charles Dickens's 1841 historical novel of that name.

clue.text: Rise to heaven, the home of the greater gods

blocks.note: to mount is to rise or climb
Olympus is used poetically for heaven, the seat of the gods

explanation.surface: A soul ascends to the heavenly dwelling of the major deities.
explanation.definitionFit: In Greek myth the twelve chief Olympian gods lived on Mount Olympus, the highest peak in Greece.

clue.text: Let off surplus dynamite, initially

indicators.note: initially points to the opening letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: spare means extra, left over
the first letter of dynamite

explanation.surface: Someone sets off leftover explosives, at least at the start.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Let off' tempts as the act of detonating, but it is the definition in its sense of excused.
explanation.definitionFit: To let someone off is to excuse them from punishment, which is to have spared them.

clue.text: Writers having a drink in a US city

blocks.note: pens are writing instruments
taken as written
cola is a fizzy soft drink

explanation.surface: Authors having a drink together in an American city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Writers' look like authors, but they are the instruments.
explanation.definitionFit: Pensacola is a port city in the Florida panhandle in the United States.

clue.text: Tins are wrong for a wine

indicators.note: letters that are wrong are out of place and must be put right

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written; it also serves in the indicator

explanation.surface: A complaint that cans are the wrong container for wine.
explanation.definitionFit: Retsina is a Greek white wine flavoured with pine resin.

clue.text: Daughter, having drunk rye after rum, becomes unsteady

indicators.note: a drunk is reeling about, so the letters of the word beside it are jumbled
after places the drunk whisky behind the word for rum, so it is sent second

blocks.note: D is the abbreviation for daughter
rum is old British slang for odd or strange
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A daughter who has drunk whisky after rum is wobbly on her feet.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drunk' and 'rum' sound like drinking; drunk is the mixing signal and rum is the adjective meaning strange.
explanation.definitionFit: Doddery describes someone shaky or tottering, usually from age.

clue.text: Splendour of Greek article under bust

indicators.note: something bust is broken, so the word before it is broken up and reassembled

blocks.note: GR is the standard abbreviation for Greek
the indefinite article
taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: The magnificence of a Greek object found beneath a sculpted bust.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Under bust' reads as a position below a statue, but 'under' is the fodder and 'bust' says to break it.
explanation.definitionFit: Grandeur and splendour are synonyms for impressive magnificence.

clue.text: Joined one editor

blocks.note: a unit is a single thing, one
ED is the usual abbreviation for editor

explanation.surface: An editor has signed up to a single organisation.
explanation.definitionFit: United and joined both describe things brought together into one.

clue.text: One-armed bandits - lost cash in 'em, stupidly

indicators.note: stupidly suggests something done without sense, so these letters are thrown into disorder

blocks.note: all twelve letters, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A gambler admits foolishly losing money in fruit machines.
explanation.definitionFit: One-armed bandit is a nickname for a gambling machine worked by a lever arm.

clue.text: Head leaving specimen, more than enough

indicators.note: the head of a word departing means its first letter is dropped

blocks.note: a sample is a specimen taken for testing

explanation.surface: A lab report: the top has been cut off a specimen, but there is plenty left.
explanation.definitionFit: Ample means plentiful, more than sufficient.

clue.text: Around five, alkie and a TT uncommonly chatty

indicators.note: around says the rearranged letters wrap about the numeral
uncommonly means in an unusual way, so these letters come out in an unusual order

blocks.note: the letters of alkie, a and TT, ready to be rearranged; and is a joining word
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: At five o'clock a drunk and a teetotaller are unusually talkative together.
explanation.walkthrough: An alkie is an alcoholic and TT means teetotal, a nice contrast in the surface; the reshuffled letters wrap round V.
explanation.definitionFit: Talkative and chatty both describe someone given to lots of conversation.

clue.text: New French calendar?

definitions.note: noun phrase standing for the adjective, as in the Revolutionary calendar

blocks.note: first meaning: radically new, innovative
second meaning: the calendar introduced in France after 1789, which named its months Brumaire, Thermidor and so on

explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that the second definition is an example: the calendar is known by this adjective rather than defined by it.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means groundbreaking and also names the calendar adopted by the French Republic in 1793.

clue.text: After surprising veto duke's dejected, defeated in the House

indicators.note: something surprising is unexpected, so the word after it turns up in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged
D abbreviates duke; the 's is a joining is
down means low in spirits

explanation.surface: A duke is downcast after an unexpected veto in the House of Lords.
explanation.definitionFit: A motion voted down has been rejected by a parliamentary vote.

clue.text: Soon converted a lone militant

indicators.note: something converted has been changed into another form, so these letters take a new shape

blocks.note: all thirteen letters, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A solitary extremist will soon be won over to the cause.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Converted' fits the surface's lone militant being radicalised or reformed, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: In no time at all is an idiom for very quickly, which is to say soon.

clue.text: Awareness, in a sense

blocks.note: taken as written
sight is one of the five senses

explanation.surface: An observation that awareness is, in a way, perception.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In a sense' reads as the hedge 'in one way', but it is IN followed by a sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Insight is a deep understanding or perception of something.

clue.text: Grey gear?

blocks.note: first meaning: colourless, without strong character
second meaning: the position of a gearbox in which no gear is engaged

explanation.walkthrough: Read together it looks like grey clothing; the question mark warns that each word is defined separately.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means drab or uncommitted, and also the gearbox setting where the engine drives nothing.

clue.text: Depend on the German rowing club

blocks.note: to lean on is to depend on
der is a German word for the

explanation.surface: Relying on a German oarsman's club.
explanation.walkthrough: Leander Club at Henley-on-Thames is one of the oldest and best-known rowing clubs in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Leander is a famous English rowing club based at Henley-on-Thames, named after the swimmer of Greek myth.

clue.text: Watch cutter pitch

blocks.note: to see is to watch
a saw is a cutting tool

explanation.surface: Watching a cricket pitch being trimmed by a mower.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pitch' suggests a sports field, but it is the verb meaning rock up and down.
explanation.definitionFit: To seesaw is to move alternately up and down, which is to pitch like a ship.

clue.text: Getting bitter with money for bread

blocks.note: a thing getting bitter is going sour
dough is slang for money

explanation.surface: Someone resents having to hand over cash for a loaf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bread' itself is slang for money, which makes the surface's money and bread look like one idea.
explanation.definitionFit: Sourdough is a kind of bread leavened with a fermented starter.

clue.text: Fish steak prepared

indicators.note: food that is prepared has been cut up and arranged, so the word before it is reworked

blocks.note: taken as written, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A menu item: a fish steak ready for cooking.
explanation.definitionFit: Skate is a flat cartilaginous sea fish, often eaten as wings.

clue.text: Wild ape is a brownish colour

indicators.note: something wild is unruly and out of control, so these letters run riot

blocks.note: the letters of both words, ready to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A wild ape turns out to be a brownish shade.
explanation.definitionFit: Sepia is a reddish-brown pigment, originally made from cuttlefish ink.

clue.text: Doctor returning to northern college

indicators.note: returning means going back the way it came, so the word for doctor is read backwards

blocks.note: to doctor is to tamper with, to rig
taken as written
N is the abbreviation for northern

explanation.surface: A physician heading back to a college in the north.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a person but is the verb meaning falsify. Girton is a college of Cambridge University.
explanation.definitionFit: Girton College is one of the constituent colleges of the University of Cambridge.

clue.text: Decidedly fashionable black suit

blocks.note: in means in fashion
spades is one of the two black suits in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A smart black suit is decidedly in style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Suit' reads as clothing, but it is a suit of playing cards.
explanation.definitionFit: In spades is an idiom meaning to a great degree, emphatically.

clue.text: Attractive young girls with special ability

blocks.note: first meaning: informal British slang for attractive people collectively
second meaning: a natural gift or flair

explanation.surface: Pretty young women who are also gifted at something.
explanation.walkthrough: In British slang, 'the local talent' means the attractive people around, a usage now dated.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a natural aptitude and, colloquially, attractive people viewed as prospects.

clue.text: Bird in box by bank

blocks.note: to spar is to box in practice
a bank is a row or tier, as of keys or oars

explanation.surface: A bird sitting in a nest box beside a river bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Box' and 'bank' read as a nest box and a riverside, but they are the verb spar and a row.
explanation.definitionFit: The sparrow is a small, common brown songbird.
